newSounds: Aspirated vs plain stops: kh/gh/th/dh/th/dh carry a puff of air, like Telugu ఖ/ఘ/థ/ధ, while k/g/t/d are unaspirated like Telugu క/గ/త/ద. Retroflex t/th/d/dh/n are pronounced with the tongue curled back, like Telugu ట/ఠ/డ/ఢ/ణ. z is z, f is f, and v is the v/w sound of Telugu వ.
rhythm: Syllable-timed, close to Telugu: every vowel is one beat, short a is a light schwa (like Telugu అ), and long aa/ee/oo stay full length (Telugu ఆ/ీ/ూ). Stress is mild and falls on the last long syllable before the end.
registerFirst: aap — the polite 'you', used with strangers and elders. tum is for friends and tu for close family or children; stick with aap until you are invited to drop it.
trap: The inherent 'a' after a consonant is a short schwa and is dropped at the end of a word: ghar is ghar, not ghara, and namaste is namaste, not namahsate. Don't add an English 'a' to every consonant, and don't trill r like a Spanish rr — Telugu ర is close.
